desc:
A simplified e-mail address has the form local@domain, with exactly one @. Return true if s follows all of these rules, otherwise false.

Local part

  • 1 to 64 characters, each a lowercase letter, a digit, ., _ or -;
  • it does not start or end with ., and it does not contain two dots in a row.

Domain

  • a list of at least two labels separated by single dots;
  • every label has 1 to 63 characters, each a lowercase letter, a digit or -, and does not start or end with -;
  • the last label (the top-level domain) consists of lowercase letters only and has at least 2 characters.

Valid: a@b.co, john.doe_1@mail-server.example.org, -x-@1.io. Invalid: a@b (one label), a..b@c.com, .a@c.com, a@-c.com, a@c.c (top-level domain too short), a@c.c0m, A@c.com (uppercase), a@@c.com.
constraints: s contains letters, digits and the characters @ . _ - +
hints: Split the string at the @ first; if the number of @ characters is not exactly one, the answer is false immediately.
Validate the local part with simple character and position checks, then split the domain on dots and validate every label.

Remember the corner cases: empty labels from a@b..com or a@.com, a label of 64 characters, a hyphen at the label edges, a top-level domain that contains digits or hyphens, and a local part of exactly 64 versus 65 characters.
editorial: The rules apply independently to the two halves, so the code splits on @ and checks each half. For the local part check the length range, the allowed alphabet, that the first and last characters are not dots, and that .. does not occur.

For the domain, split on dots. Fewer than two labels fails. Every label (an empty one from consecutive dots fails the length check) must have 1-63 characters from the label alphabet and must not begin or end with a hyphen. Finally, the last label must be made of letters only and be at least two long. Doing the checks in a fixed order and returning early keeps the code short.
The total work is proportional to the length of the string.
